items.title: A map that vanishes on a set of points vanishes at every point of its closure
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the propagation of the vanishing of a base changed map from a set of points to its closure at source lines 1647-1662, label lemma-F-zero-somewhat-closed-points, whose proof occupies source lines 1664-1689. The proof reduces the geometric statement to an algebra statement in two steps that both need care: the vanishing is checked etale locally on the fibre, so one passes to an etale neighbourhood on which the source becomes projective over the base while still covering the chosen point of the fibre, and the closure condition is preserved because an etale morphism is open, so the chosen point remains in the closure of the image of the set. The algebra statement is then settled with the ideal attached to the map and its vanishing locus. The counted statement records neither the etale neighbourhood nor the transfer of the closure condition.
